title: Seasonal Influenza Vaccination Policies for Poultry Workers in 33 Pan American Health Organization Member States in 2026: A Review
abstract: Background/Objective: Since 2004, seasonal influenza vaccination has been technically recommended for poultry workers as a public health measure to reduce the risk of co-infection with human and avian influenza viruses and the potential emergence of reassortant strains. The Latin America and the Caribbean (LAC) region has co-circulation of seasonal and avian influenza, with outbreaks in different animal species, including humans. Also, LAC is a major poultry-producing region, with large workforces exposed to domestic poultry, increasing opportunities for virus transmission at the human–animal interface. This review aimed to describe the current state of seasonal influenza vaccination policies across 33 LAC countries and to identify which countries explicitly mention poultry workers. Methods: We conducted a literature review with structured and iterative search strategies from the electronic Joint Reporting Form on Immunization (eJRF) and the national health authorities’ websites of the 33 countries. Results: As of July 2026, eight countries explicitly included poultry workers among the target groups for seasonal influenza vaccination: Chile, Costa Rica, Cuba, Ecuador, Guatemala, Honduras, Peru and Uruguay. In contrast, 14 countries did not mention poultry workers in their most recent vaccination policies available online. For 11 countries, no publicly available data was identified. Conclusions: Substantial gaps exist in the adoption and reporting of seasonal influenza vaccination policies for poultry workers across the LAC region. Most of the region’s major poultry-producing countries do not specifically target this group, nor do most of the countries where outbreaks of avian influenza were recorded. This represents a missed opportunity to strengthen prevention efforts at the human–animal interface.

analysis.summary_en: This review examines seasonal influenza vaccination policies for poultry workers across 33 Pan American Health Organization member states. It identifies that eight countries explicitly include poultry workers in their vaccination policies, while 14 do not mention them, and 11 have no publicly available data. The review highlights significant gaps in policy adoption and reporting, particularly in major poultry-producing countries and those with avian influenza outbreaks. These gaps represent a missed opportunity to enhance prevention at the human–animal interface. The findings underscore the need for improved surveillance, documentation, and implementation of targeted vaccination strategies for poultry workers to reduce co-infection risks and prevent reassortant strain emergence.

abstract_zh: 背景/目的:自2004年以来,季节性流感 疫苗接种已被推荐作为家禽从业人员的公共卫生措施,以降低人类和禽流感病毒共感染的风险以及潜在的重组病毒株出现的可能性。拉丁美洲和加勒比地区(LAC)同时存在季节性流感和禽流感的共循环,暴发在不同动物物种中传播,包括人类。此外,LAC是主要的家禽生产地区,拥有大量接触家禽的劳动力,增加了病毒在人类与动物界面传播的机会。本综述旨在描述33个LAC国家当前的季节性流感 疫苗接种政策状况,并确定哪些国家明确将家禽从业人员列为目标群体。方法:我们通过从电子联合免疫报告表(eJRF)和33个国家的国家卫生部门网站进行结构化和迭代的文献检索策略,开展了文献综述。结果:截至2026年7月,有8个国家明确将家禽从业人员列为季节性流感 疫苗接种的目标群体:智利、哥斯达黎加、古巴、厄瓜多尔、危地马拉、洪都拉斯、秘鲁和乌拉圭。相比之下,有14个国家在其最近可在线获取的疫苗接种政策中未提及家禽从业人员。对于另外11个国家,未找到公开的可用数据。结论:在LAC地区,家禽从业人员季节性流感 疫苗接种政策的采纳和报告存在显著差距。大多数该地区的主要家禽生产国并未特别针对这一群体,也未在记录禽流感暴发的国家中特别提及。这代表了在人类与动物界面加强预防措施的错失机会。

title: Increased circulation of influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 viruses with reduced susceptibility to oseltamivir, Germany 2024-2026.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Oseltamivir is still considered to be the first-line antiviral treatment for severe seasonal influenza. However, resistance to neuraminidase (NA) inhibitors poses significant challenges to influenza management. Since the 2023/24 season, A(H1N1)pdm09 viruses carrying neuraminidase substitutions (NA-I223V and/or NA-S247N) have emerged in Germany, other EU/EEA countries, and some of the World Health Organization (WHO) regions. These viruses have been linked to reduced oseltamivir susceptibility. METHODS: A rapid RT-PCR/pyrosequencing assay was developed and validated to detect NA-I223X and NA-S247X substitutions. Subsequently, a total of 765 A(H1N1)pdm09 viruses detected in Germany during the 2024/25 and 2025/26 influenza seasons were characterized phenotypically using fluorometric NA inhibition testing and/or genotypically using next-generation sequencing and pyrosequencing. RESULTS: The prevalence of A(H1N1)pdm09 viruses bearing the NA-S247N substitution increased from 1.2% in the 2024/25 season to 56.8% in the 2025/26 season, accounting for up to 80% of analyzed viruses by March 2026. Viruses carrying NA-S247N exhibited higher oseltamivir IC50 values than wild-type viruses. Combinations of NA-S247N with substitutions at position 223 demonstrated an additional increase. In viruses carrying the combined NA-S247N and NA-I223V/T substitutions oseltamivir showed reduced inhibition with increased IC50 values of up to 17-fold compared to wild type viruses. CONCLUSIONS: The accumulation of NA substitutions in A(H1N1)pdm09 influenza viruses, particularly NA-S247N in combination with NA-I223V/T, substantially reduces susceptibility to oseltamivir. The marked increase in NA-S247N prevalence suggests that this substitution is becoming persistent rather than transient. Targeted pyrosequencing is a practical tool for the early detection of emerging resistance-associated substitutions.

title_zh: 德国2024-2026年流感甲型H1N1流感病毒pdm09病毒循环增加且对奥司他韦耐药性降低。
source_body_en: BACKGROUND: Oseltamivir is still considered to be the first-line antiviral treatment for severe seasonal influenza. However, resistance to neuraminidase (NA) inhibitors poses significant challenges to influenza management. Since the 2023/24 season, A(H1N1)pdm09 viruses carrying neuraminidase substitutions (NA-I223V and/or NA-S247N) have emerged in Germany, other EU/EEA countries, and some of the World Health Organization (WHO) regions. These viruses have been linked to reduced oseltamivir susceptibility. METHODS: A rapid RT-PCR/pyrosequencing assay was developed and validated to detect NA-I223X and NA-S247X substitutions. Subsequently, a total of 765 A(H1N1)pdm09 viruses detected in Germany during the 2024/25 and 2025/26 influenza seasons were characterized phenotypically using fluorometric NA inhibition testing and/or genotypically using next-generation sequencing and pyrosequencing. RESULTS: The prevalence of A(H1N1)pdm09 viruses bearing the NA-S247N substitution increased from 1.2% in the 2024/25 season to 56.8% in the 2025/26 season, accounting for up to 80% of analyzed viruses by March 2026. Viruses carrying NA-S247N exhibited higher oseltamivir IC50 values than wild-type viruses. Combinations of NA-S247N with substitutions at position 223 demonstrated an additional increase. In viruses carrying the combined NA-S247N and NA-I223V/T substitutions oseltamivir showed reduced inhibition with increased IC50 values of up to 17-fold compared to wild type viruses. CONCLUSIONS: The accumulation of NA substitutions in A(H1N1)pdm09 influenza viruses, particularly NA-S247N in combination with NA-I223V/T, substantially reduces susceptibility to oseltamivir. The marked increase in NA-S247N prevalence suggests that this substitution is becoming persistent rather than transient. Targeted pyrosequencing is a practical tool for the early detection of emerging resistance-associated substitutions.
abstract_zh: 背景:奥司他韦仍被认为是严重季节性流感的首选抗病毒药物 治疗。然而,对神经氨酸酶(NA)抑制剂的耐药性给流感管理带来了重大挑战。自2023/24流感季以来,德国、其他欧盟/欧洲经济区国家以及世界卫生组织(WHO)部分地区的流感甲型H1N1流感病毒pdm09病毒中出现了携带神经氨酸酶替代位点(NA-I223V和/或NA-S247N)的病毒株,这些病毒株与奥司他韦耐药性降低有关。方法:开发并验证了一种快速RT-PCR/焦磷酸测序检测方法,用于检测NA-I223X和NA-S247X替代位点。随后,通过荧光神经氨酸酶抑制试验和/或下一代测序和焦磷酸测序对德国2024/25和2025/26流感季中检测到的765株甲型H1N1流感病毒pdm09病毒进行了表型和基因型特征分析。结果:携带NA-S247N替代位点的甲型H1N1流感病毒pdm09病毒的患病率从2024/25流感季的1.2%上升至2025/26流感季的56.8%,到2026年3月为止,这些病毒占分析病毒的最高比例达80%。携带NA-S247N替代位点的病毒表现出比野生型病毒更高的奥司他韦IC50值。当NA-S247N与223位点的替代位点结合时,耐药性进一步增加,其IC50值最高可达野生型病毒的17倍。结论:流感甲型H1N1流感病毒pdm09病毒中神经氨酸酶替代位点的积累,特别是NA-S247N与NA-I223V/T的组合,显著降低了奥司他韦的敏感性。NA-S247N的显著增加表明该替代位点正在变得持续存在而非暂时现象。靶向焦磷酸测序是一种实用工具,可用于早期检测与耐药性相关的新兴替代位点。

title: Molecular Epidemiology and Evolution of Swine Influenza A Viruses, Vietnam, 2020-2024.
abstract: Swine influenza A viruses (IAV-S) caused the 2009 H1N1 pandemic and pose a future zoonotic and pandemic threat. Vietnam represents a critical hotspot for IAV-S emergence within East and Southeast Asia, with dense swine and human populations and intensive livestock trade. We conducted genomic surveillance of IAV-S in Vietnam during 2020-2024, extending previous surveillance from 2013-2019. We identified multiple co-circulating H1 and H3 clades, including pandemic H1N1, Eurasian avian-like, and European lineages, by conducting phylogenetic analysis of 56 IAV-S isolates (21 H1N1, 31 H1N2, and 4 H3N2). Three H1 clades persisted exclusively in Vietnam, circulating up to 12 years. Phylogeographic analysis revealed multiple independent introduction events from North America, Europe, China, Thailand, and Cambodia. We detected extensive reassortment that frequently involved pandemic H1N1 virus internal genes. We identified several lineage-specific mutations associated with mammalian adaptation. Our findings underscore the ongoing IAV-S evolution and need for sustained surveillance in Vietnam.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to understand the molecular epidemiology and evolution of swine influenza A viruses (IAV-S) in Vietnam, addressing the ongoing threat of IAV-S as a zoonotic and pandemic risk. Vietnam, with its dense swine and human populations and intensive livestock trade, is a critical hotspot for IAV-S emergence.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved genomic surveillance of IAV-S in Vietnam from 2020 to 2024, extending previous surveillance from 2013 to 2019. The research covered multiple co-circulating H1 and H3 clades, including pandemic H1N1, Eurasian avian-like, and European lineages, from 56 IAV-S isolates (21 H1N1, 31 H1N2, and 4 H3N2).
analysis.methods: Genomic surveillance was conducted by phylogenetic and phylogeographic analysis of 56 IAV-S isolates. The study identified multiple co-circulating clades and extensive reassortment involving pandemic H1N1 virus internal genes. Lineage-specific mutations associated with mammalian adaptation were also identified.
analysis.main_results: The study identified multiple co-circulating H1 and H3 clades, including pandemic H1N1, Eurasian avian-like, and European lineages, from 56 IAV-S isolates. Phylogeographic analysis revealed multiple independent introduction events from North America, Europe, China, Thailand, and Cambodia. Extensive reassortment involving pandemic H1N1 virus internal genes was detected, and several lineage-specific mutations associated with mammalian adaptation were identified.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study's findings underscore the ongoing evolution of IAV-S in Vietnam, highlighting the need for sustained surveillance. Novel mutations and reassortment events were identified, providing insights into the virus's adaptation to mammalian hosts.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings have implications for surveillance, diagnosis, and understanding the potential for future zoonotic and pandemic threats. They emphasize the importance of continued monitoring of IAV-S in Vietnam and other regions with dense swine and human populations.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's limitations include the potential for sampling bias and the need for further research to understand the full impact of identified mutations and reassortment events. The evidence strength is moderate due to the observational nature of the study and the need for longitudinal data to confirm the significance of the findings.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在了解猪流感A病毒(IAV-S)在越南的分子进化和传播特征,应对IAV-S作为动物源性和大流行风险的持续威胁。越南因其密集的猪和人类人口以及活跃的畜牧业贸易,是IAV-S出现的关键热点。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究涉及对2020年至2024年期间越南的IAV-S进行分子分析,扩展了此前2013年至2019年的研究。研究覆盖了多个共循环的H1和H3分支,包括大流行H1N1、欧亚禽源样和欧洲谱系,共分析了56株IAV-S分离株(21株H1N1、31株H1N2和4株H3N2)。
elements_zh.methods: 分子分析通过分析56株IAV-S分离株的系统发育和系统发育地理特征进行。研究鉴定了多个共循环的分支,并检测到涉及大流行H1N1病毒内部基因的广泛基因重配。还鉴定了与哺乳动物适应相关的多个谱系特异性特征。
elements_zh.main_results: 研究鉴定了多个共循环的H1和H3分支,包括大流行H1N1、欧亚禽源样和欧洲谱系,来自56株IAV-S分离株。系统发育地理分析揭示了来自北美、欧洲、中国、泰国和柬埔寨的多次独立引入事件。检测到涉及大流行H1N1病毒内部基因的广泛基因重配,并鉴定了与哺乳动物适应相关的多个谱系特异性特征。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果强调了IAV-S在越南持续传播的特征,突显了需要持续监测的重要性。识别了新的特征和基因重配事件,为病毒适应哺乳动物宿主提供了见解。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果对监测、基因组监测以及理解未来动物源性和大流行威胁的潜力具有重要意义。它们强调了在越南及其他猪和人类人口密集地区持续监测IAV-S的重要性。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究的局限性包括可能存在抽样偏差,以及需要进一步研究以了解所识别特征和基因重配事件的全部影响。由于研究的观察性质和缺乏纵向数据,证据强度中等,需进一步确认研究结果的重要性。

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to understand the molecular epidemiology and evolution of swine influenza A viruses (IAV-S) in Vietnam, addressing the ongoing threat of IAV-S as a zoonotic and pandemic risk. Vietnam, with its dense swine and human populations and intensive livestock trade, is a critical hotspot for IAV-S emergence.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: The study involved genomic surveillance of IAV-S in Vietnam from 2020 to 2024, extending previous surveillance from 2013 to 2019. The research covered multiple co-circulating H1 and H3 clades, including pandemic H1N1, Eurasian avian-like, and European lineages, from 56 IAV-S isolates (21 H1N1, 31 H1N2, and 4 H3N2).
analysis_en.methods: Genomic surveillance was conducted by phylogenetic and phylogeographic analysis of 56 IAV-S isolates. The study identified multiple co-circulating clades and extensive reassortment involving pandemic H1N1 virus internal genes. Lineage-specific mutations associated with mammalian adaptation were also identified.
analysis_en.main_results: The study identified multiple co-circulating H1 and H3 clades, including pandemic H1N1, Eurasian avian-like, and European lineages, from 56 IAV-S isolates. Phylogeographic analysis revealed multiple independent introduction events from North America, Europe, China, Thailand, and Cambodia. Extensive reassortment involving pandemic H1N1 virus internal genes was detected, and several lineage-specific mutations associated with mammalian adaptation were identified.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The study's findings underscore the ongoing evolution of IAV-S in Vietnam, highlighting the need for sustained surveillance. Novel mutations and reassortment events were identified, providing insights into the virus's adaptation to mammalian hosts.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings have implications for surveillance, diagnosis, and understanding the potential for future zoonotic and pandemic threats. They emphasize the importance of continued monitoring of IAV-S in Vietnam and other regions with dense swine and human populations.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's limitations include the potential for sampling bias and the need for further research to understand the full impact of identified mutations and reassortment events. The evidence strength is moderate due to the observational nature of the study and the need for longitudinal data to confirm the significance of the findings.

title_zh: 猪流感A病毒在越南的分子进化和传播特征,2020-2024年。
source_body_en: Swine influenza A viruses (IAV-S) caused the 2009 H1N1 pandemic and pose a future zoonotic and pandemic threat. Vietnam represents a critical hotspot for IAV-S emergence within East and Southeast Asia, with dense swine and human populations and intensive livestock trade. We conducted genomic surveillance of IAV-S in Vietnam during 2020-2024, extending previous surveillance from 2013-2019. We identified multiple co-circulating H1 and H3 clades, including pandemic H1N1, Eurasian avian-like, and European lineages, by conducting phylogenetic analysis of 56 IAV-S isolates (21 H1N1, 31 H1N2, and 4 H3N2). Three H1 clades persisted exclusively in Vietnam, circulating up to 12 years. Phylogeographic analysis revealed multiple independent introduction events from North America, Europe, China, Thailand, and Cambodia. We detected extensive reassortment that frequently involved pandemic H1N1 virus internal genes. We identified several lineage-specific mutations associated with mammalian adaptation. Our findings underscore the ongoing IAV-S evolution and need for sustained surveillance in Vietnam.
abstract_zh: 猪流感A病毒(IAV-S)引发了2009年的H1N1大流行,并对未来的动物源性和大流行威胁构成潜在风险。越南是东亚和东南亚地区IAV-S出现的关键热点,拥有密集的猪和人类人口以及活跃的畜牧业贸易。我们对2020-2024年期间越南的IAV-S进行了分子分析,扩展了此前2013-2019年的研究。通过分析56株IAV-S分离株(21株H1N1、31株H1N2和4株H3N2),我们鉴定了多个共循环的H1和H3分支,包括大流行H1N1、欧亚禽源样和欧洲谱系。三个H1分支仅在越南持续存在,循环时间长达12年。系统发育地理分析揭示了来自北美、欧洲、中国、泰国和柬埔寨的多次独立引入事件。我们检测到广泛的基因重配,经常涉及大流行H1N1病毒的内部基因。我们还鉴定了与哺乳动物适应相关的多个谱系特异性特征。研究结果强调了IAV-S在越南持续存在的传播特征,并突显了需要持续监测的重要性。

analysis.research_question_and_background: Annual influenza vaccination is recommended for all persons ≥6 months old without a contraindication.1-6 The study addresses the need for updated vaccination guidelines based on the current season's influenza viruses.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study is a review of the 2026-2027 influenza season, focusing on seasonal influenza viruses in the US. It includes all persons ≥6 months old without contraindications to vaccination.
analysis.methods: The methods involve reviewing influenza vaccines available this season in the US, as listed in Table 3. The study does not include detailed statistical or laboratory procedures.
analysis.main_results: The main results include the listing of influenza vaccines available for the 2026-2027 season in the US. No specific numerical findings or statistical results are reported.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that annual influenza vaccination remains a critical public health measure. The novelty lies in the updated vaccine recommendations for the current season.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform public health recommendations for seasonal influenza vaccination and highlight the importance of updated vaccine formulations for effective prevention.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on a review of available vaccines and does not include detailed data on vaccine efficacy or outcomes. The evidence is moderate as it relies on existing guidelines rather than new empirical data.

analysis.summary_en: This study provides updated recommendations for seasonal influenza vaccination in the US for the 2026-2027 season. It emphasizes the importance of annual vaccination for all individuals aged ≥6 months without contraindications. The main results include the listing of available vaccines, which are based on the current circulating influenza viruses. The authors interpret that vaccination remains a key public health strategy, with the novelty being the specific vaccine formulations recommended for the season. The findings have implications for public health practice, particularly in ensuring vaccine coverage and effectiveness. However, the study is limited by its reliance on existing guidelines rather than new empirical data, resulting in moderate evidence strength.

title: Distinct Longitudinal Antibody Responses Following Primary Influenza Infection or Vaccination in Infants: A Prospective Birth Cohort Study
abstract: The longitudinal effects of initial influenza exposure on the magnitude, persistence, and antigen specificity of antibody responses during infancy remain incompletely understood. We investigated humoral antibody responses following primary influenza infection or seasonal vaccination in a prospective US birth cohort with weekly respiratory surveillance for influenza infection. Influenza-specific serum IgG binding to H1 and H3 haemagglutinin (HA) antigens, HA inhibition (HAI), and live-virus neutralizing antibody responses were assessed longitudinally. To minimize the influence of maternally derived antibodies, analyses of primary exposure responses were restricted to infants for whom influenza-specific maternal antibodies had declined below the assay detection limit before exposure. Antibody responses were compared following primary infection and vaccination and examined after subsequent annual vaccination. We found that maternal influenza-specific IgG declined rapidly during early infancy. Among infants without detectable pre-exposure influenza-specific antibodies, primary influenza infection was associated with greater post-exposure antibody responses and less measurable decline over follow-up than primary vaccination. These groups differed in age, calendar season, and exposure characteristics, limiting direct attribution of these differences to the route of exposure. In infants with previous influenza infection followed by vaccination, responses after subsequent vaccination initially showed greater binding to the previously infecting subtype among the tested HA antigens. With repeated vaccination, responses became more distributed across the tested antigens. Our findings reveal differences in the magnitude, persistence, and antigen specificity of antibody responses according to the nature and sequence of influenza exposure. By prospectively capturing early-life exposures, this study provides longitudinal evidence linking exposure history to subsequent humoral antibody responses.

analysis.summary_en: This study explores the longitudinal antibody responses in infants following primary influenza infection or vaccination, focusing on seasonal influenza viruses. The research aimed to understand how exposure to influenza through infection or vaccination affects the magnitude, persistence, and antigen specificity of antibody responses during early life. The study was conducted in a prospective US birth cohort with weekly respiratory surveillance. Antibody responses were measured using assays for IgG binding, HA inhibition, and neutralizing antibodies. Results showed that maternal influenza-specific IgG declined rapidly during early infancy, and infants exposed to influenza through infection had greater post-exposure antibody responses compared to those vaccinated. Additionally, responses in infants with prior infection followed by vaccination showed initial preference for the previously infecting subtype but became more distributed with repeated vaccination. The study highlights the importance of exposure history in shaping antibody responses and provides insights into the immune dynamics of infants. However, the study's groups differed in age, season, and exposure characteristics, which limits the ability to directly attribute differences to the route of exposure. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the observational nature of the study and potential confounding factors.

abstract_zh: 初次流感暴露对婴儿期抗体反应的强度、持续时间和抗原特异性所产生的纵向影响仍不完全清楚。我们在一项前瞻性美国出生队列研究中调查了婴儿在初次流感感染或季节性流感暴露后体液抗体反应的情况,该研究每周对流感感染进行呼吸道监测。纵向评估了针对H1和H3血凝素(HA)抗原的流感特异性血清IgG结合反应、血凝素抑制(HAI)反应以及活病毒中和抗体反应。为减少母源抗体的影响,初次暴露反应的分析仅限于那些在暴露前流感特异性母源抗体已降至检测限以下的婴儿。比较了初次感染和流感暴露后的抗体反应,并在随后的年度流感暴露后进行了检查。我们发现,母源流感特异性IgG在婴儿早期迅速下降。在那些暴露前未检测到流感特异性抗体的婴儿中,初次流感感染与暴露后的抗体反应强度更大,且在随访期间下降更不明显,而初次流感暴露则表现出不同的情况。这些群体在年龄、日历季节和暴露特征上存在差异,限制了将这些差异直接归因于暴露途径。对于先前感染过流感病毒后又经历流感暴露的婴儿,在随后的流感暴露中,其抗体反应最初对之前感染的亚型表现出更强的结合能力。随着重复的流感暴露,抗体反应逐渐分布到所测试的抗原中。我们的研究结果揭示了根据流感暴露的性质和顺序,抗体反应的强度、持续时间和抗原特异性存在差异。通过前瞻性地记录生命早期的暴露情况,本研究提供了将暴露史与随后体液抗体反应联系起来的纵向证据。

title: Real-time situational assessment of respiratory virus epidemics in Australia over winter 2025 and an out-of-season influenza A H3N2 epidemic
abstract: Introduction: In temperate regions, influenza and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) typically exhibit seasonal epidemics during the winter months, often concurrently with SARS-CoV-2 epidemics. Monitoring past and real-time trends in infection dynamics is important for informing public health situational awareness, including identifying and characterising unusual epidemic activity. However, data used to monitor these trends can exhibit substantial noise including strong day-of-the-week variation in reporting. In addition, case data for influenza can obscure distinct trends in influenza subtypes if not combined with virological data. Aim: By quantifying trends in respiratory virus activity using statistical methods, the Australia–Aotearoa Consortium for Epidemic Forecasting and Analytics (ACEFA) aims to provide government partners with comprehensive epidemic intelligence. Methods: Analyses were performed on daily case time series data for SARS-CoV-2, RSV and influenza across Australia's eight jurisdictions. Past and real-time trends were inferred for each pathogen and each influenza subtype using Bayesian p-spline models. Results: The 2025 Winter Situational Assessment Program provided weekly reports throughout the winter season and during the out-of-season influenza A H3N2 epidemic, driven by the emergence of the novel influenza subclade ('subclade K'). Despite limited subtyping data, our analysis provided an early signal of increasing influenza A H3N2 during a period in which overall influenza cases were decreasing; increases in influenza A H3N2 activity were first detected in July, and by mid-August, increasing H3N2 activity was estimated across all jurisdictions. Discussion: Our analysis highlights the benefits of incorporating statistical methods into real-time epidemic situational assessment and in consolidating reporting across jurisdictions.

abstract_zh: 引言:在温带地区,流感和呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)通常在冬季表现出季节性流行,常与SARS-CoV-2流行同时发生。监测过去和实时的感染动态趋势对于提升公共卫生态势感知能力至关重要,包括识别和描述异常的流行活动。然而,用于监测这些趋势的数据可能包含大量噪声,包括报告中的强周日效应。此外,如果未结合病毒学数据,流感病例数据可能会掩盖流感亚型中的不同趋势。目标:通过使用统计方法量化呼吸道病毒活动趋势,澳大利亚-新西兰流行预测与分析联盟(ACEFA)旨在为政府合作伙伴提供全面的流行病学情报。方法:分析了澳大利亚八个司法管辖区每日的SARS-CoV-2、RSV和流感病例时间序列数据。使用贝叶斯p样条模型对每种病原体和每种流感亚型的过去和实时趋势进行了推断。结果:2025年冬季态势评估计划在整个冬季季节以及非季节性甲型H3N2流感暴发期间提供了每周报告,这一暴发由新型流感亚群('亚群K')的出现所驱动。尽管亚型数据有限,我们的分析在整体流感病例下降期间提供了早期信号,表明甲型H3N2流感活动正在增加;甲型H3N2活动的增加最早在7月被检测到,到8月中旬,所有司法管辖区均估计出现增加趋势。讨论:我们的分析突显了在实时流行态势评估中整合统计方法以及在各司法管辖区整合报告的益处。

title: Dual Antiviral and Immunomodulatory Effects of Phytochemicals in Influenza A Virus Infection: Targeting Key Host Signaling Pathways.
abstract: Influenza A virus (IAV) remains a major public health threat due to its high genetic variability and ability to evade host immune responses. While antiviral drugs and vaccines remain the key measures against influenza infection, their limited efficacy and the emergence of resistant viral strains have prompted growing interest in exploring complementary therapeutic approaches. In this review, we critically evaluate current evidence on how plant-derived compounds modulate innate immune signaling networks, including toll-like receptor, retinoic acid-inducible gene I, mitogen-activated protein kinase, and nuclear factor kappa B pathways during IAV infection. We further address the pathway cross-talk that underpins this broad immunomodulatory activity, the translational barriers including bioavailability, metabolic transformation, and standardization that currently limit clinical progression, and the mechanistic gaps that future studies must resolve. Collectively, this review argues that phytocompounds should be understood as modulators of an integrated innate immune network, an insight that reframes both their therapeutic potential and the experimental standards required to advance them.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores the dual antiviral and immunomodulatory effects of phytochemicals in influenza A virus (IAV) infection, focusing on seasonal human IAV strains such as A(H1N1)pdm09, A(H3N2), B/Victoria, and B/Yamagata. It evaluates how plant-derived compounds modulate key host signaling pathways, including toll-like receptor, retinoic acid-inducible gene I, mitogen-activated protein kinase, and nuclear factor kappa B. The review highlights the importance of understanding these compounds as modulators of an integrated innate immune network, while also addressing the translational barriers and mechanistic gaps that limit their clinical application. The findings suggest that further research is needed to resolve these gaps and improve the standardization of phytochemicals for therapeutic use.

title_zh: 流感A病毒感染中双抗病毒药物和植物化学物的免疫调节作用:靶向关键宿主信号通路。
source_body_en: Influenza A virus (IAV) remains a major public health threat due to its high genetic variability and ability to evade host immune responses. While antiviral drugs and vaccines remain the key measures against influenza infection, their limited efficacy and the emergence of resistant viral strains have prompted growing interest in exploring complementary therapeutic approaches. In this review, we critically evaluate current evidence on how plant-derived compounds modulate innate immune signaling networks, including toll-like receptor, retinoic acid-inducible gene I, mitogen-activated protein kinase, and nuclear factor kappa B pathways during IAV infection. We further address the pathway cross-talk that underpins this broad immunomodulatory activity, the translational barriers including bioavailability, metabolic transformation, and standardization that currently limit clinical progression, and the mechanistic gaps that future studies must resolve. abstract_zh: 流感A病毒(IAV)由于其高度的遗传变异性和逃避宿主 免疫应答的能力,仍然是一个重要的公共卫生威胁。尽管抗病毒药物药物和疫苗仍是应对流感感染的关键措施,但其有限的疗效以及耐药病毒株的出现促使人们日益关注探索互补的治疗方案。在本综述中,我们批判性地评估了当前关于植物来源化合物如何调节先天免疫信号网络的证据,包括在IAV感染期间的Toll样受体、视黄酸诱导基因I、丝裂原活化蛋白激酶和核因子κB通路。我们进一步探讨了支撑这种广泛免疫调节活性的通路交叉对话,以及目前限制其临床进展的翻译障碍,包括生物利用度、代谢转化和标准化问题,同时指出了未来研究必须解决的机制性空白。总体而言,本综述认为植物化学物应被理解为整合先天免疫网络的调节因子,这一观点重新定义了它们的治疗潜力以及推进其应用所需的实验标准。

title: Navigating the Transition to RNA-Based Influenza Vaccines: A State-of-the-Art Review
abstract: Seasonal influenza and the ongoing emergence of zoonotic influenza viruses, including highly pathogenic avian influenza A (H5N1), remain substantial global public health threats, underscoring the need for rapidly adaptable vaccine platforms. This state-of-the-art review critically evaluates the clinical development of RNA-based influenza vaccines through a comprehensive assessment of ClinicalTrials.gov records and peer-reviewed literature. Candidates were examined across four domains: seasonal influenza vaccines, pre-pandemic influenza vaccines, combination respiratory vaccines, and self-amplifying RNA (saRNA) platforms. Clinical evidence indicates that mRNA influenza vaccines consistently elicit robust humoral immune responses and, in late-stage trials, have demonstrated improved relative efficacy against influenza A compared with conventional influenza vaccines. Reactogenicity is generally more frequent with mRNA vaccines, particularly with respect to transient mild-to-moderate systemic adverse events. However, serious adverse events remain uncommon and broadly comparable to those observed with licensed comparator vaccines. Pre-pandemic and multicomponent mRNA vaccine candidates similarly demonstrate strong immunogenicity, supporting the potential of RNA platforms for both seasonal vaccination and pandemic preparedness. Clinical development of saRNA influenza vaccines has progressed through early-phase trials, although publicly available clinical data remain limited. Regulatory milestones in 2026, including U.S. approval of mRNA-1010 (mFlusiva), the first approved mRNA-based seasonal influenza vaccine, and European Union authorization of mRNA-1083 (mCOMBRIAX), an mRNA-based influenza-COVID-19 combination vaccine, represent important steps in the clinical transition and implementation of RNA-based influenza vaccination.

title_zh: RNA基流感疫苗疫苗:前沿综述
source_body_en: Seasonal influenza and the ongoing emergence of zoonotic influenza viruses, including highly pathogenic avian influenza A (H5N1), remain substantial global public health threats, underscoring the need for rapidly adaptable vaccine platforms. This state-of-the-art review critically evaluates the clinical development of RNA-based influenza vaccines through a comprehensive assessment of ClinicalTrials.gov records and peer-reviewed literature. Candidates were examined across four domains: seasonal influenza vaccines, pre-pandemic influenza vaccines, combination respiratory vaccines, and self-amplifying RNA (saRNA) platforms. Clinical evidence indicates that mRNA influenza vaccines consistently elicit robust humoral immune responses and, in late-stage trials, have demonstrated improved relative efficacy against influenza A compared with conventional influenza vaccines. Reactogenicity is generally more frequent with mRNA vaccines, particularly with respect to transient mild-to-moderate systemic adverse events. However, serious adverse events remain uncommon and broadly comparable to those observed with licensed comparator vaccines. Pre-pandemic and multicomponent mRNA vaccine candidates similarly demonstrate strong immunogenicity, supporting the potential of RNA platforms for both seasonal vaccination and pandemic preparedness. Clinical development of saRNA influenza vaccines has progressed through early-phase trials, although publicly available clinical data remain limited. Regulatory milestones in 2026, including U.S. approval of mRNA-1010 (mFlusiva), the first approved mRNA-based seasonal influenza vaccine, and European Union authorization of mRNA-1083 (mCOMBRIAX), an mRNA-based influenza-COVID-19 combination vaccine, represent important steps in the clinical transition and implementation of RNA-based influenza vaccination.

title: E protein-driven iNKT subset modulation shapes early immune responses during influenza A virus infection.
abstract: Invariant natural killer T (iNKT) cells play a critical role in the early phases of the response to influenza A virus (IAV) infection by influencing inflammation and immune regulation, but the impact of the different iNKT functional subsets (iNKT1, iNKT2, and iNKT17) in these responses is unclear. We used genetically altered mouse strains with normal numbers of iNKT cells but different iNKT subset representation (NKTWT and NKTET2) to analyze the impact of different iNKT functional subsets on IAV infection outcomes. We show that IAV-infected NKTET2 mice have reduced weight loss, diminished myeloid recruitment and activation, and a 40% reduction in lung-infected areas compared with controls. This was accompanied by lower expression of inflammatory mediators (Ifna, Isg15, Ifit1) and chemoattractants Ccl2 and Cxcl2, along with elevated levels of type III interferon (Ifnl3). Single-cell RNA sequencing analysis of iNKTs suggests that these changes are driven by quantitative differences in iNKT responses, which are predominantly type I in NKTWT mice but type 17 in NKTET2 mice. These differences correlate with higher levels of Il22b and Il1b in NKTET2 mice lungs. Altogether, our results indicate that changes in iNKT subset representation impact the outcome of IAV infections by changing the character of the early immune response, and suggests that selective activation of iNKT subsets could be used to improve vaccination strategies in the future.

analysis.summary_en: This study explores how different iNKT functional subsets influence the early immune response to influenza A virus (IAV) infection. title_zh: E蛋白驱动的iNKT亚群调控塑造了流感A病毒感染早期的免疫应答.
source_body_en: Invariant natural killer T (iNKT) cells play a critical role in the early phases of the response to influenza A virus (IAV) infection by influencing inflammation and immune regulation, but the impact of the different iNKT functional subsets (iNKT1, iNKT2, and iNKT17) in these responses is unclear. We used genetically altered mouse strains with normal numbers of iNKT cells but different iNKT subset representation (NKTWT and NKTET2) to analyze the impact of different iNKT functional subsets on IAV infection outcomes. We show that IAV-infected NKTET2 mice have reduced weight loss, diminished myeloid recruitment and activation, and a 40% reduction in lung-infected areas compared with controls. This was accompanied by lower expression of inflammatory mediators (Ifna, Isg15, Ifit1) and chemoattractants Ccl2 and Cxcl2, along with elevated levels of type III interferon (Ifnl3). Single-cell RNA sequencing analysis of iNKTs suggests that these changes are driven by quantitative differences in iNKT responses, which are predominantly type I in NKTWT mice but type 17 in NKTET2 mice. These differences correlate with higher levels of Il22b and Il1b in NKTET2 mice lungs. Altogether, our results indicate that changes in iNKT subset representation impact the outcome of IAV infections by changing the character of the early immune response, and suggests that selective activation of iNKT subsets could be used to improve vaccination strategies in the future.
abstract_zh: 不变的自然杀伤T细胞(iNKT细胞)在流感A病毒(IAV)感染的早期阶段通过影响炎症和免疫调节发挥关键作用,但不同iNKT功能亚群(iNKT1、iNKT2和iNKT17)对这些反应的影响尚不清楚。我们使用了具有正常iNKT细胞数量但不同iNKT亚群比例的基因改造小鼠品系(NKTWT和NKTET2)来分析不同iNKT功能亚群对IAV感染结果的影响。我们发现,感染IAV的NKTET2小鼠表现出体重减轻减少、髓系细胞招募和激活减弱,以及与对照组相比肺部感染区域减少了40%。这些变化伴随着炎症介质(Ifna、Isg15、Ifit1)和趋化因子Ccl2和Cxcl2的表达降低,以及III型干扰素(Ifnl3)水平的升高。对iNKT细胞的单细胞RNA测序分析表明,这些变化是由iNKT反应的定量差异驱动的,其中NKTWT小鼠的iNKT反应主要为I型,而NKTET2小鼠的iNKT反应则主要为17型。这些差异与NKTET2小鼠肺部Il22b和Il1b水平的升高相关。总体而言,我们的结果表明,iNKT亚群比例的变化通过改变早期免疫应答的特征来影响IAV感染的结果,并提示未来可以选择性激活iNKT亚群以改善疫苗接种策略。

title: A-099 Development of Human and Avian Influenza Analytical Reference Materials for Surveillance and Diagnostics
abstract: Abstract Abstract Development of Human and Avian Influenza Analytical Reference Materials for Surveillance and Diagnostics Holly Ann Asbury, BS; Jason Bose; Victoria Knight-Connoni, PhD; Leka Papazisi, DVM, PhD Background Human and highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) viruses pose a significant public health threat, with the potential to cause widespread illness and economic losses. Early detection and control of outbreaks depend on effective surveillance and diagnostic testing. Method ATCC® developed a comprehensive suite of quantitative synthetic analytical reference materials (ARMs) for HPAI virus serotypes H5N1, H5N6, H7N7, H7N9, and H9N2; human influenza A virus serotypes H1N1, H3N2, and H1N1 2009 pandemic; and Influenza B virus strains. Each synthetic ARM contains the complete sequences from segments 4, 5, 6, 7, and 8, including the HA, NP, NA, M1, M2, NS1, and NEP/NS1 genes, covering 50% of the influenza genome. These segments are key diagnostic targets for molecular tests and provide sufficient genomic context for assessing assay specificity. These ARMs are manufactured using a highly reliable synthetic biology technology, verified by next-generation sequencing, and quantified via digital-based PCR. Further, they do not contain any viable material and can be handled in BSL-1 settings. As such, they are intended to serve as safe and reliable positive controls for molecular tests for surveillance and diagnostics. Results These synthetic ARMs were experimentally evaluated using several published quantitative PCR (qPCR) assays, including those from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), the World Health Organization (WHO), and the World Organization for Animal Health (WOAH). Additionally, the avian influenza ARMs were confirmed to be compatible with subtype-specific loop-mediated isothermal amplification (LAMP) assays and the BioFire Diagnostics FilmArray (bioMérieux) in vitro diagnostic device. We conducted an in silico assessment of ARM compatibility using over 250 published assays. The synthetic products performed as well as genomic RNA in all tests. Conclusions The data show that all synthetic ARMs for avian and human influenza are effectively designed and suitable for developing and validating molecular detection and quantification assays. Moreover, our findings indicate that the synthetic RNA ARMs are equivalent to their corresponding genomic RNA, making them a valuable BSL-1 alternative to BSL-3–derived materials. Our results suggest that these synthetic ARMs can serve as reliable and safe controls for molecular assays used in diagnostics and surveillance.

analysis.summary_en: This study describes the development of synthetic analytical reference materials (ARMs) for human and avian influenza viruses, focusing on their utility as safe and reliable positive controls for molecular diagnostic assays. The ARMs were designed for key influenza virus serotypes, including HPAI H5N1, H5N6, H7N9, H9N2, human influenza A(H1N1)pdm09, A(H3N2), and B virus strains. The synthetic materials were manufactured using synthetic biology and verified by next-generation sequencing and digital-based PCR. They were experimentally evaluated against multiple published qPCR assays and found to perform as well as genomic RNA. Additionally, they were confirmed compatible with LAMP assays and the BioFire FilmArray device. The study concludes that these synthetic ARMs are effectively designed and suitable for developing and validating molecular detection and quantification assays, offering a BSL-1 alternative to BSL-3 materials. The findings highlight the potential of synthetic ARMs to enhance safety and reliability in influenza diagnostics and surveillance. The evidence does not report any specific limitations to the study design or its strength.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 人类和高致病性禽流感(HPAI)病毒对公共卫生构成重大威胁,可能引发广泛疾病和经济损失。早期检测和控制暴发依赖于有效的监测和诊断测试。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: ATCC®为高致病性禽流感病毒血清型H5N1、H5N6、H7N7、H7N9和H9N2;人类流感A病毒血清型H1N1、H3N2和2009年大流行H1N1;以及流感B病毒株开发了一套全面的定量合成分析参考材料(ARMs)。这些ARMs旨在作为监测和诊断分子测试的安全且可靠的阳性对照。
elements_zh.methods: 这些ARMs使用高度可靠的合成生物学技术制造,通过下一代测序进行验证,并通过基于数字的PCR进行量化。这些片段是分子检测测试的关键诊断目标,并提供了足够的基因组背景以评估检测特异性。结果 这些合成ARMs通过多种已发表的定量PCR(qPCR)检测方法进行了实验评估,包括来自疾病控制与预防中心(CDC)、世界卫生组织(WHO)和世界动物卫生组织(WOAH)的方法。我们还使用超过250种已发表的检测方法进行了ARMs兼容性的计算机模拟评估。
elements_zh.main_results: 合成产品在所有测试中均表现与基因组RNA相当。此外,禽流感ARMs被证实与亚型特异性环介导等温扩增(LAMP)检测方法以及BioFire Diagnostics FilmArray(bioMérieux)体外诊断设备兼容。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 数据表明,所有用于禽流感和人类流感的合成ARMs都设计良好,适合用于开发和验证分子检测和量化检测方法。我们的研究结果表明,合成RNA ARMs与相应的基因组RNA等效,使其成为BSL-3衍生材料的有价值的BSL-1替代品。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些合成ARMs可以作为诊断和监测中使用的分子检测方法的可靠和安全的对照。它们提供了BSL-3衍生材料的BSL-1替代方案,提高了诊断检测的安全性和可及性。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 所提供的证据未报告任何具体的研究设计或证据强度的局限性。

abstract_zh: 摘要 为监测和诊断开发人类和禽流感分析参考材料 Holly Ann Asbury,BS;Jason Bose;Victoria Knight-Connoni,PhD;Leka Papazisi,DVM,PhD 背景 人类和高致病性禽流感(HPAI)病毒对公共卫生构成重大威胁,可能引发广泛疾病和经济损失。早期检测和控制暴发依赖于有效的监测和诊断测试。方法 ATCC®为高致病性禽流感病毒血清型H5N1、H5N6、H7N7、H7N9和H9N2;人类流感A病毒血清型H1N1、H3N2和2009年大流行H1N1;以及流感B病毒株开发了一套全面的定量合成分析参考材料(ARMs)。每种合成ARM包含来自第4、5、6、7和8段的完整序列,包括HA、NP、NA、M1、M2、NS1和NEP/NS1基因,覆盖了50%的流感基因组。这些片段是分子检测测试的关键诊断目标,并提供了足够的基因组背景以评估检测特异性。这些ARMs使用高度可靠的合成生物学技术制造,通过下一代测序进行验证,并通过基于数字的PCR进行量化。此外,这些材料不含任何活性成分,可在BSL-1环境下处理。因此,它们旨在作为监测和诊断分子测试的安全且可靠的阳性对照。结果 这些合成ARMs通过多种已发表的定量PCR(qPCR)检测方法进行了实验评估,包括来自疾病控制与预防中心(CDC)、世界卫生组织(WHO)和世界动物卫生组织(WOAH)的方法。此外,禽流感ARMs被证实与亚型特异性环介导等温扩增(LAMP)检测方法以及BioFire Diagnostics FilmArray(bioMérieux)体外诊断设备兼容。我们还使用超过250种已发表的检测方法进行了ARMs兼容性的计算机模拟评估。合成产品在所有测试中均表现与基因组RNA相当。结论 数据表明,所有用于禽流感和人类流感的合成ARMs都设计良好,适合用于开发和验证分子检测和量化检测方法。此外,我们的研究结果表明,合成RNA ARMs与相应的基因组RNA等效,使其成为BSL-3衍生材料的有价值的BSL-1替代品。我们的结果表明,这些合成ARMs可以作为诊断和监测中使用的分子检测方法的可靠和安全的对照。

title: Network analysis of correlated conformational dynamics across the evolution of influenza A virus NS1
abstract: Protein evolution requires sequence changes to alter molecular properties without disrupting the dynamic organization necessary for function. How residue-level networks of correlated motions accommodate such mutations remains poorly understood. Here, we investigate the evolution of correlated conformational dynamics in nonstructural protein 1 (NS1) variants of influenza A viruses that emerged between 1918 and 2004. From molecular dynamics (MD) simulations we built residue networks in which edge weights reflect generalized correlations of conformational motion. The network of correlated dynamics is characterized using centrality analysis. Overall network properties are well-conserved across NS1 variants, indicating evolutionary robustness of the dynamical network. Residues ranked highly across multiple centrality measures form a predominantly hydrophobic cluster in the protein core. These residues exhibited low conformational entropy and high sequence conservation, consistent with rigid, coordinated motions. In contrast, residues exhibiting large differences in betweenness and closeness centrality ranks occupied flexible, solvent-exposed regions surrounding the core network. These residues also showed lower evolutionary conservation. These findings reveal a core-periphery structure in which a rigid hydrophobic network enables long-range dynamic connectivity while more adaptable peripheral regions accommodate evolutionary sequence variation. This architecture provides a mechanistic framework for long-range epistatic interactions without compromising the underlying structural framework.

Here, we investigate the evolution of correlated conformational dynamics in nonstructural protein 1 (NS1) variants of influenza A viruses that emerged between 1918 and 2004. From molecular dynamics (MD) simulations we built residue networks in which edge weights reflect generalized correlations of conformational motion. The network of correlated dynamics is characterized using centrality analysis. Overall network properties are well-conserved across NS1 variants, indicating evolutionary robustness of the dynamical network. Residues ranked highly across multiple centrality measures form a predominantly hydrophobic cluster in the protein core. These residues exhibited low conformational entropy and high sequence conservation, consistent with rigid, coordinated motions. In contrast, residues exhibiting large differences in betweenness and closeness centrality ranks occupied flexible, solvent-exposed regions surrounding the core network. These residues also showed lower evolutionary conservation. These findings reveal a core-periphery structure in which a rigid hydrophobic network enables long-range dynamic connectivity while more adaptable peripheral regions accommodate evolutionary sequence variation. This architecture provides a mechanistic framework for long-range epistatic interactions without compromising the underlying structural framework.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to understand how residue-level networks of correlated motions in influenza A virus NS1 variants accommodate mutations while maintaining functional dynamics. The background highlights the need to explore sequence changes that alter molecular properties without disrupting the dynamic organization essential for function.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study investigated the evolution of correlated conformational dynamics in nonstructural protein 1 (NS1) variants of influenza A viruses that emerged between 1918 and 2004. It focused on the structural and functional properties of these variants across different time periods.
analysis.methods: The researchers used molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to build residue networks, where edge weights reflected generalized correlations of conformational motion. They characterized the network using centrality analysis to identify key residues and their roles in dynamic connectivity.
analysis.main_results: The network of correlated dynamics was found to be well-conserved across NS1 variants, indicating evolutionary robustness. Residues ranked highly in multiple centrality measures formed a predominantly hydrophobic cluster in the protein core, showing low conformational entropy and high sequence conservation.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings reveal a core-periphery structure in NS1, where a rigid hydrophobic network enables long-range dynamic connectivity, while more adaptable peripheral regions allow for evolutionary sequence variation. This architecture provides a mechanistic framework for long-range epistatic interactions without compromising the structural framework.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The study offers insights into the structural dynamics of influenza A virus NS1, which could inform future research on viral evolution and the development of targeted interventions for seasonal influenza.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study relies on molecular dynamics simulations and centrality analysis, which may not fully capture in vivo dynamics. The evidence is moderate, as it is based on computational models rather than experimental validation.

analysis.summary_en: This study explores the evolution of correlated conformational dynamics in the NS1 protein of influenza A viruses from 1918 to 2004. Using molecular dynamics simulations, the researchers built residue networks to analyze dynamic connectivity and identified a core-periphery structure. The core consists of a rigid, hydrophobic cluster with low conformational entropy and high sequence conservation, while the periphery includes flexible, solvent-exposed regions with lower evolutionary conservation. These findings suggest that the structural framework of NS1 is evolutionarily robust, enabling long-range interactions while allowing for sequence variation. The study provides a mechanistic understanding of how influenza A virus NS1 maintains function through dynamic organization, which could inform future research on viral evolution and seasonal influenza. However, the reliance on computational models limits the confidence in the results, and the evidence is considered moderate.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究调查了1918年至2004年间出现的流感A病毒非结构蛋白1(NS1)变体中相关构象动态的进化。它关注了这些变体在不同时期的结构和功能特性。
elements_zh.methods: 研究人员使用分子动力学(MD)模拟构建了残基网络,其中边权重反映了构象运动的广义相关性。他们通过中心性分析来表征网络,以确定关键残基及其在动态连接中的作用。
elements_zh.main_results: 相关动态网络在NS1变体中被发现保持良好一致性,表明其具有进化稳健性。在多种中心性指标中排名较高的残基形成了蛋白质核心中的主要疏水簇,表现出较低的构象熵和较高的序列保守性。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些发现揭示了NS1中的核心-边缘结构,其中刚性的疏水网络使长程动态连接成为可能,而更具适应性的边缘区域则容纳了进化序列变化。这种架构为长程表型相互作用提供了机制框架,而不会损害其基础结构框架。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 本研究提供了对流感A病毒NS1结构动态的见解,这可能有助于未来关于病毒进化的研究以及针对季节性流感的定向干预措施的开发。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究依赖于分子动力学模拟和中心性分析,这可能无法完全捕捉体内动态。证据强度中等,因为它是基于计算模型而非实验验证。

abstract_zh: 蛋白进化需要序列变化来改变分子特性,同时不破坏其功能所必需的动态组织。如何在残基水平的相关运动网络中容纳这样的突变仍不清楚。在这里,我们研究了1918年至2004年间出现的流感A病毒非结构蛋白1(NS1)变体中相关构象动态的进化。通过分子动力学(MD)模拟,我们构建了残基网络,其中边权重反映了构象运动的广义相关性。使用中心性分析来表征相关动态网络。整体网络特性在NS1变体中保持良好一致性,表明动态网络具有进化稳健性。在多种中心性指标中排名较高的残基形成了蛋白质核心中的主要疏水簇。这些残基表现出较低的构象熵和较高的序列保守性,与刚性、协调的运动一致。相比之下,表现出之间性与接近性中心性排名较大差异的残基占据了围绕核心网络的灵活、溶剂暴露区域。这些残基也显示出较低的进化保守性。这些发现揭示了NS1中一个核心-边缘结构,其中刚性的疏水网络使长程动态连接成为可能,而更具适应性的边缘区域则容纳了进化序列变化。这种架构为长程表型相互作用提供了机制框架,而不会损害其基础结构框架。

title: VirPLM: antigenic prediction of influenza A/H3N2 viruses with a fine-tuned protein language model.
abstract: MOTIVATION: Human influenza A/H3N2 viruses undergo rapid antigenic evolution primarily driven by the hemagglutinin subunit 1 (HA1). Within HA1, amino acid substitutions under immune pressure cause antigenic drift, necessitating frequent updates to vaccine strains. While hemagglutination inhibition (HI) assays remain the gold standard for assessing antigenic relationships, their labor-intensive and low-throughput nature limits scalability. Fortunately, the rapid accumulation of HA1 sequences enables sequence-based antigenic prediction, yet effectively extracting informative representations from these viral sequences remains challenging. RESULTS: In this study, we present VirPLM, a two-stage framework that adapts the ESM-2 protein language model to H3N2 HA1 sequences for antigenic prediction. VirPLM significantly outperforms representative methods and maintains robust performance under both cross-validation and retrospective time-split evaluations. Moreover, VirPLM identifies highly critical sites enriched in known regions related to antigenic evolution. In the season-specific coverage analysis, VirPLM-prioritized strains achieve higher estimated coverage rates than the corresponding historical strains recommended by the World Health Organization in most evaluated seasons, suggesting that VirPLM can provide complementary sequence-based evidence for candidate strain prioritization. AVAILABILITY AND IMPLEMENTATION: The source code is available at https://github.com/xingyili/VirPLM, and the version used in this study is archived in Zenodo (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.21650323).

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the challenge of antigenic prediction for influenza A/H3N2 viruses, which undergo rapid antigenic evolution due to immune pressure on the hemagglutinin subunit 1 (HA1).
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study developed and evaluated a two-stage framework called VirPLM for antigenic prediction of influenza A/H3N2 viruses using HA1 sequences, with performance assessed through cross-validation and retrospective time-split evaluations.
analysis.methods: VirPLM adapts the ESM-2 protein language model to H3N2 HA1 sequences to predict antigenic properties, leveraging the rapid accumulation of HA1 sequences to create informative representations for antigenic drift analysis.
analysis.main_results: VirPLM significantly outperforms representative methods in antigenic prediction and identifies highly critical sites associated with antigenic evolution. In season-specific coverage analysis, strains prioritized by VirPLM achieve higher estimated coverage rates than historical WHO-recommended strains in most evaluated seasons.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret VirPLM as a novel tool that provides complementary sequence-based evidence for candidate strain prioritization, enhancing the accuracy and scalability of antigenic prediction for seasonal influenza.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that VirPLM can improve the selection of vaccine strains by offering a more accurate and scalable method for antigenic prediction, which has direct implications for vaccine development and public health preparedness.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's evidence is strong, as it demonstrates robust performance across multiple evaluation methods, but the framework's generalizability to other influenza subtypes or contexts may be limited without further validation.

analysis.summary_en: This study introduces VirPLM, a two-stage framework that uses a fine-tuned protein language model to predict antigenic properties of influenza A/H3N2 viruses. The research addresses the challenge of antigenic evolution driven by immune pressure on HA1, which necessitates frequent vaccine updates. VirPLM outperforms existing methods in cross-validation and time-split evaluations, identifying critical sites for antigenic drift. The framework's ability to prioritize strains with higher coverage rates than historical WHO recommendations highlights its potential to improve vaccine strain selection. While the results are promising, the study's focus on H3N2 limits its generalizability to other influenza subtypes. The findings offer a scalable and accurate method for antigenic prediction, which could enhance vaccine development and public health strategies for seasonal influenza.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在解决流感A/H3N2病毒抗原预测的挑战,这些病毒由于血凝素亚单位1(HA1)上的免疫压力而经历快速抗原漂移。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究开发并评估了一个名为VirPLM的两阶段框架,用于基于HA1序列预测流感A/H3N2病毒的抗原特性,其性能通过交叉验证和回顾性时间分割评估进行评估。
elements_zh.methods: VirPLM通过将ESM-2蛋白质语言模型适应于H3N2 HA1序列来预测抗原特性,利用HA1序列的快速积累创建信息性表示以进行抗原漂移分析。
elements_zh.main_results: VirPLM在抗原预测方面显著优于代表性方法,并识别出与抗原漂移高度相关的关键位点。在季节性覆盖分析中,VirPLM优先选择的毒株在大多数评估季节中估计覆盖率高于历史WHO推荐的毒株。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将VirPLM解释为一种新颖的工具,能够为候选毒株优先选择提供互补的基于序列的证据,从而提高抗原预测的准确性和可扩展性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,VirPLM可以通过提供更准确和可扩展的抗原预测方法,改进抗原漂移毒株的选择,这对抗原漂移疫苗的开发和公共卫生准备具有直接意义。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究的证据是强有力的,因为它在多种评估方法中均表现出稳健的性能,但该框架在其他流感亚型或情境下的泛化能力可能受到限制,除非进一步验证。

abstract_zh: MOTIVATION: 人类流感A/H3N2病毒由于血凝素亚单位1(HA1)上的免疫压力而经历快速抗原漂移。在HA1中,氨基酸替换导致抗原漂移,需要频繁更新抗原漂移毒株。尽管血凝素抑制(HI)试验仍然是评估抗原关系的黄金标准,但其劳动密集型和低通量的性质限制了其可扩展性。幸运的是,HA1序列的快速积累使得基于序列的抗原预测成为可能,但有效提取这些病毒序列中的信息性表示仍然是一个挑战。RESULTS: 在本研究中,我们提出了VirPLM,这是一个两阶段框架,通过将ESM-2蛋白质语言模型适应于H3N2 HA1序列来进行抗原预测。VirPLM在抗原预测方面显著优于代表性方法,并且在交叉验证和回顾性时间分割评估中均表现出稳健的性能。此外,VirPLM识别出与抗原漂移高度相关的关键位点。在季节性覆盖分析中,VirPLM优先选择的毒株在大多数评估季节中估计覆盖率高于世界卫生组织推荐的历史毒株,这表明VirPLM可以为候选毒株优先选择提供互补的基于序列的证据。AVAILABILITY AND IMPLEMENTATION: 源代码可在https://github.com/xingyili/VirPLM获取,本研究中使用的版本已存档于Zenodo(DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.21650323)。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在解决流感A/H3N2病毒抗原预测的挑战,这些病毒由于血凝素亚单位1(HA1)上的免疫压力而经历快速抗原漂移。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究开发并评估了一个名为VirPLM的两阶段框架,用于基于HA1序列预测流感A/H3N2病毒的抗原特性,其性能通过交叉验证和回顾性时间分割评估进行评估。
analysis_zh.methods: VirPLM通过将ESM-2蛋白质语言模型适应于H3N2 HA1序列来预测抗原特性,利用HA1序列的快速积累创建信息性表示以进行抗原漂移分析。
analysis_zh.main_results: VirPLM在抗原预测方面显著优于代表性方法,并识别出与抗原漂移高度相关的关键位点。在季节性覆盖分析中,VirPLM优先选择的毒株在大多数评估季节中估计覆盖率高于历史WHO推荐的毒株。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将VirPLM解释为一种新颖的工具,能够为候选毒株优先选择提供互补的基于序列的证据,从而提高抗原预测的准确性和可扩展性。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,VirPLM可以通过提供更准确和可扩展的抗原预测方法,改进抗原漂移毒株的选择,这对抗原漂移疫苗的开发和公共卫生准备具有直接意义。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究的证据是强有力的,因为它在多种评估方法中均表现出稳健的性能,但该框架在其他流感亚型或情境下的泛化能力可能受到限制,除非进一步验证。

title: A Dominant Genome-Wide Amino-Acid Signature Characterizes the Global Expansion of Influenza A(H3N2) Clade K
abstract: Abstract In late 2025, influenza A(H3N2) Clade K viruses increased in frequency in global surveillance datasets. To characterize the molecular pattern associated with this emergence, we conducted genome-wide analysis of viruses collected during December 2025–January 2026 using geographically stratified sampling and a database-wide historical comparison with A(H3N2) sequences from 2019–2024. Predominant amino-acid substitutions were identified across multiple protein-coding open reading frames (ORF), including polymerase, surface, matrix, nucleoprotein, and nonstructural proteins. Historical database-wide analysis showed marked heterogeneity in the frequencies of these amino-acid states during 2019–2024, ranging from absent or rare to already highly prevalent. To examine their joint occurrence, polymorphic amino-acid states across the analyzed ORF were combined into genome-wide composite amino-acid signatures. Among 1,255 viruses with complete eight-segment sequence data, 168 distinct signatures were identified. A single signature predominated, occurring in 744 (59.3%) viruses, whereas the second most frequent signature occurred in 139 (11.1%); the remaining signatures were substantially less frequent. These findings demonstrate that the global emergence of influenza A(H3N2) Clade K was characterized by a predominant genome-wide amino-acid signature assembled from amino-acid states with markedly different historical frequencies. Genome-wide analysis of composite molecular signatures provides an additional framework for characterizing the genetic structure of rapidly expanding influenza virus populations.

Predominant amino-acid substitutions were identified across multiple protein-coding open reading frames (ORF), including polymerase, surface, matrix, nucleoprotein, and nonstructural proteins. Historical database-wide analysis showed marked heterogeneity in the frequencies of these amino-acid states during 2019–2024, ranging from absent or rare to already highly prevalent. To examine their joint occurrence, polymorphic amino-acid states across the analyzed ORF were combined into genome-wide composite amino-acid signatures. Among 1,255 viruses with complete eight-segment sequence data, 168 distinct signatures were identified. A single signature predominated, occurring in 744 (59.3%) viruses, whereas the second most frequent signature occurred in 139 (11.1%); the remaining signatures were substantially less frequent. These findings demonstrate that the global emergence of influenza A(H3N2) Clade K was characterized by a predominant genome-wide amino-acid signature assembled from amino-acid states with markedly different historical frequencies. Genome-wide analysis of composite molecular signatures provides an additional framework for characterizing the genetic structure of rapidly expanding influenza virus populations.
title_original: A Dominant Genome-Wide Amino-Acid Signature Characterizes the Global Expansion of Influenza A(H3N2) Clade K

abstract_zh: 摘要 2025年底,流感甲型H3N2流感病毒克隆K病毒在全球监测数据集中的频率增加。为了表征这种出现的分子模式,我们使用地理分层抽样方法,对2025年12月至2026年1月期间收集的病毒进行了基因组广泛分析,并与2019年至2024年的甲型H3N2流感病毒序列进行了数据库范围的历史比较。在多个蛋白质编码开放阅读框(ORF)中,包括聚合酶、表面、基质、核蛋白和非结构蛋白,均鉴定出主要的氨基酸取代。历史数据库范围分析显示,在2019年至2024年期间,这些氨基酸状态的频率存在显著的异质性,从缺失或罕见到已经高度流行。为了检查它们的共同出现,分析的ORF中的多态性氨基酸状态被组合成基因组广泛复合氨基酸特征。在1255株具有完整八段序列数据的病毒中,共鉴定出168种不同的特征。其中一种特征占主导地位,出现在744株(59.3%)病毒中,而第二常见的特征出现在139株(11.1%);其余特征的频率显著较低。这些发现表明,流感甲型H3N2流感病毒克隆K的全球出现特征是通过一种主导的基因组广泛氨基酸特征实现的,该特征由具有显著不同历史频率的氨基酸状态组成。对复合分子特征进行基因组广泛分析为表征快速扩张的流感病毒种群的遗传结构提供了额外的框架。

title: Myeloid cell expression of the VDR and parathyroid hormone control the host response to influenza infection in mice
abstract: Introduction Respiratory infections caused by seasonal influenza viruses remain a major global health burden. Vitamin D receptor (VDR) signaling regulates immune responses, but the role of the VDR and its interaction with parathyroid hormone (PTH) in host resistance to H1N1 influenza infection is not understood. Methods Global VDR knockout (KO) mice, or myeloid (M) deletion of the VDR (M-VDR KO) and the respective wildtype (WT) littermates were infected with H1N1 influenza virus. Additional experiments treated WT mice with intermittent PTH or vehicle and then infected them with a H1N1 influenza A virus. Disease severity, mortality, viral burden and clearance, lung pathology, and inflammatory cytokine responses were evaluated. Results H1N1 influenza infection of WT mice resulted in non-lethal disease, whereas VDR KO mice had 21% mortality, delayed viral clearance, more severe symptoms and lung pathology. The increased severity of respiratory disease was accompanied by higher type I and II interferon responses in the lungs. M-VDR KO mice had increased disease severity and delayed viral clearance compared to WT littermates. PTH-treated WT mice had increased clinical scores, influenza M gene, and cytokine responses compared to vehicle treated WT mice. Discussion The work describes a novel paradigm in which the vitamin D-PTH axis governs host resistance to influenza virus disease by controlling the amount of inflammation and the amount of virus in the lung. In addition, the data suggest that VDR expression in myeloid cells is critical for controlling the early innate immune response to influenza viruses.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to understand the role of the vitamin D receptor (VDR) and parathyroid hormone (PTH) in host resistance to influenza infection, addressing a knowledge gap in the immunological response to influenza viruses.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study used global VDR knockout (KO) mice, myeloid VDR deletion (M-VDR KO) mice, and their wildtype (WT) littermates, infected with H1N1 influenza virus. Additional experiments involved treating WT mice with intermittent PTH or vehicle and then infecting them with a H1N1 influenza A virus.
analysis.methods: The study employed global VDR KO mice, myeloid VDR deletion mice, and WT littermates. Infection with H1N1 influenza virus was performed, and additional experiments involved treating WT mice with PTH or vehicle.
analysis.main_results: H1N1 influenza infection in WT mice resulted in non-lethal disease, whereas VDR KO mice had 21% mortality, delayed viral clearance, more severe symptoms and lung pathology. M-VDR KO mice also had increased disease severity and delayed viral clearance compared to WT littermates. PTH-treated WT mice had increased clinical scores, influenza M gene, and cytokine responses compared to vehicle-treated WT mice.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The work describes a novel paradigm in which the vitamin D-PTH axis governs host resistance to influenza virus disease by controlling the amount of inflammation and the amount of virus in the lung. VDR expression in myeloid cells is critical for controlling the early innate immune response to influenza viruses.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that targeting the vitamin D-PTH axis could be a potential strategy for managing influenza infection, particularly in individuals with VDR deficiency in myeloid cells. This could have implications for the development of new therapeutic approaches and understanding the immune response to influenza.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by the use of animal models, which may not fully represent human responses. The sample size was small, and the study did not include direct comparisons with human influenza infection.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the role of vitamin D receptor (VDR) and parathyroid hormone (PTH) in host resistance to influenza infection using mouse models. It found that VDR deficiency in myeloid cells led to increased disease severity and delayed viral clearance, while PTH treatment enhanced the immune response. These findings suggest potential therapeutic strategies for managing influenza infection.

elements_zh.main_results: H1N1流感病毒感染WT小鼠导致非致命性疾病,而VDR KO小鼠出现21%的死亡率,病毒清除延迟,症状和肺部病理更严重。与WT同窝小鼠相比,M-VDR KO小鼠也表现出更高的疾病严重程度和病毒清除延迟。与接受载体处理的WT小鼠相比,接受PTH处理的WT小鼠临床评分、流感M基因和细胞因子反应均增加。

abstract_zh: 引言 由季节性流感病毒引起的呼吸道感染仍然是全球主要的健康负担。维生素D受体(VDR)信号调控免疫应答,但VDR及其与甲状旁腺激素(PTH)的相互作用在宿主抵抗H1N1流感病毒感染中的作用尚不清楚。方法 使用全球VDR敲除(KO)小鼠、髓系(M)VDR敲除(M-VDR KO)小鼠及其相应的野生型(WT)同窝小鼠感染H1N1流感病毒。另外,实验还对WT小鼠进行间歇性PTH或载体处理,随后感染H1N1流感A病毒。评估了疾病严重程度、死亡率、病毒载量和清除、肺部病理以及炎症细胞因子反应。结果 H1N1流感病毒感染WT小鼠导致非致命性疾病,而VDR KO小鼠出现21%的死亡率,病毒清除延迟,症状和肺部病理更严重。呼吸系统疾病严重程度的增加伴随着肺部I型和II型干扰素反应的升高。M-VDR KO小鼠与WT同窝小鼠相比,疾病严重程度增加且病毒清除延迟。接受PTH处理的WT小鼠与接受载体处理的WT小鼠相比,临床评分、流感M基因和细胞因子反应均增加。讨论 本研究描述了一种新的范式,即维生素D-PTH轴通过调控肺部炎症程度和病毒量来控制宿主对流感病毒疾病的抵抗力。此外,数据表明,髓系细胞中VDR的表达对于控制流感病毒的早期先天免疫应答至关重要。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在了解维生素D受体(VDR)和甲状旁腺激素(PTH)在宿主抵抗流感病毒感染中的作用,填补了对流感病毒免疫应答的知识空白。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究使用了全球VDR敲除(KO)小鼠、髓系VDR敲除(M-VDR KO)小鼠及其相应的野生型(WT)同窝小鼠,并感染了H1N1流感病毒。另外,实验还涉及对WT小鼠进行间歇性PTH或载体处理,随后感染H1N1流感A病毒。
analysis_zh.methods: 本研究采用全球VDR敲除(KO)小鼠、髓系VDR敲除小鼠及其野生型(WT)同窝小鼠。进行了H1N1流感病毒感染,并对WT小鼠进行了PTH或载体处理的额外实验。
analysis_zh.main_results: H1N1流感病毒感染WT小鼠导致非致命性疾病,而VDR KO小鼠出现21%的死亡率,病毒清除延迟,症状和肺部病理更严重。与WT同窝小鼠相比,M-VDR KO小鼠也表现出更高的疾病严重程度和病毒清除延迟。与接受载体处理的WT小鼠相比,接受PTH处理的WT小鼠临床评分、流感M基因和细胞因子反应均增加。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 本研究描述了一种新的范式,即维生素D-PTH轴通过调控肺部炎症程度和病毒量来控制宿主对流感病毒疾病的抵抗力。髓系细胞中VDR的表达对于控制流感病毒的早期先天免疫应答至关重要。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,针对维生素D-PTH轴可能是一种管理流感感染的潜在策略,特别是在髓系细胞中存在VDR缺乏的个体中。这可能对开发新的治疗方案以及理解流感病毒的免疫应答具有重要意义。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究的局限性在于使用了动物模型,这可能无法完全代表人类的反应。样本量较小,且未包括与人类流感感染的直接比较。

title: Forecasting Seasonal Influenza Patterns and Trends Using Historical Data and Time Series Analysis
abstract: Abstract Effective forecasting of seasonal influenza patterns is crucial for public health preparedness, as influenza remains a recurrent threat with considerable morbidity and mortality, especially among vulnerable populations. The virus's high mutation rate and the emergence of new strains complicate accurate prediction of outbreak timing and severity, despite ongoing surveillance efforts. Early detection and robust influenza surveillance are essential for equipping healthcare systems to respond and for alleviating the seasonal strain on resources. This study leverages historical data and time series analysis to identify patterns in influenza spread and predict outbreak peaks. Key findings reveal that incorporating multivariate and ensemble forecasting models—such as autoregressive integrated moving average (ARIMA), Bayesian inference, and machine learning approaches—substantially improves prediction accuracy. Notably, combining epidemiological data with search engine trends and environmental variables yields a more comprehensive and real-time forecast model, enabling more accurate and timely predictions. These methods also capture regional variations and can adapt to emerging trends, increasing the robustness of outbreak preparedness. The significance of this research lies in its potential to enhance public health response by enabling early detection and resource allocation, improving vaccination timing, and ultimately reducing influenza-related morbidity and mortality. With influenza remaining a persistent global threat, this study’s approach underscores the importance of integrating advanced predictive tools and real-time data in epidemiological forecasting, providing a foundation for more effective health intervention strategies.

title_zh: 利用历史数据和时间序列分析预测季节性流感模式和趋势
source_body_en: Abstract Effective forecasting of seasonal influenza patterns is crucial for public health preparedness, as influenza remains a recurrent threat with considerable morbidity and mortality, especially among vulnerable populations. The virus's high mutation rate and the emergence of new strains complicate accurate prediction of outbreak timing and severity, despite ongoing surveillance efforts. Early detection and robust influenza surveillance are essential for equipping healthcare systems to respond and for alleviating the seasonal strain on resources. This study leverages historical data and time series analysis to identify patterns in influenza spread and predict outbreak peaks. Key findings reveal that incorporating multivariate and ensemble forecasting models—such as autoregressive integrated moving average (ARIMA), Bayesian inference, and machine learning approaches—substantially improves prediction accuracy. Notably, combining epidemiological data with search engine trends and environmental variables yields a more comprehensive and real-time forecast model, enabling more accurate and timely predictions. These methods also capture regional variations and can adapt to emerging trends, increasing the robustness of outbreak preparedness. The significance of this research lies in its potential to enhance public health response by enabling early detection and resource allocation, improving vaccination timing, and ultimately reducing influenza-related morbidity and mortality. With influenza remaining a persistent global threat, this study’s approach underscores the importance of integrating advanced predictive tools and real-time data in epidemiological forecasting, providing a foundation for more effective health intervention strategies.
abstract_zh: 摘要 有效预测季节性流感模式对于公共卫生准备至关重要,因为流感仍然是一个反复出现的威胁,具有显著的发病率和死亡率,尤其是在易感人群中。尽管持续进行监测工作,该病毒的高突变率以及新毒株的出现使得准确预测暴发的时间和严重程度变得复杂。早期检测和强大的流感监测对于使医疗系统能够做出响应以及缓解季节性资源压力至关重要。本研究利用历史数据和时间序列分析来识别流感传播模式并预测暴发峰值。关键发现表明,结合多元和集成预测模型——如自回归积分滑动平均(ARIMA)、贝叶斯推断和机器学习方法——显著提高了预测的准确性。值得注意的是,将流行病学数据与搜索引擎趋势和环境变量相结合,可以构建一个更全面且实时的预测模型,从而实现更准确和及时的预测。这些方法还能捕捉地区差异并适应新兴趋势,提高暴发准备的稳健性。本研究的意义在于其潜在能力,可以增强公共卫生响应,实现早期检测和资源分配,改善疫苗接种时间安排,最终减少与流感相关的发病率和死亡率。由于流感仍然是一个持续的全球性威胁,本研究的方法强调了在流行病学预测中整合先进预测工具和实时数据的重要性,为更有效的健康干预策略奠定了基础。

title: Correlation of seasonal influenza rates with hospital-acquired Clostridioides difficile rates: Implications for research and interventions for prevention
abstract: Introduction: Hospital-acquired Clostridioides difficile infection (HA-CDI) rate variability can create challenges for assessing interventions that might improve rates. We therefore sought to assess whether seasonal trends in HA-CDI could be related to influenza rates by examining the sensitivity and applicability of statistical methods that identify seasonal trend associations. Methods: We assessed HA-CDI rates per 10,000 patient-days and influenza hospitalizations per 1,000 admissions in four acute care facilities from January 2016 to December 2018. Four statistical approaches were used in R (4.5.1) including (1) autoregressive integrated moving average (ARIMA); (2) cross-correlation to assess if dependencies lagged over time; (3) Poisson harmonic regression to model cyclical trends; and (4) Poisson harmonic regression models including influenza rates. Results: ARIMA approaches did not detect seasonality in HA-CDI rates, but found strong seasonality in the influenza rates, whereas cross-correlation analysis found evidence of correlation between the series at a lag of zero (R = 0.41, 95% CI 0.08 to 0.65) and provided an indication of a seasonal relationship. Poisson harmonic regression for trends suggested that influenza rates predicted CDI rates ( p p p Conclusions: Poisson harmonic regression provided a sensitive means of identifying seasonality in HA-CDI rates with the seasonality effect being accounted for by influenza admission rates, which may be mediated by inappropriate antibiotic prescriptions. This observation may be useful in interpreting future interventions to reduce HA-CDI.
journal: Journal of the Association of Medical Microbiology and Infectious Disease Canada

title: N6-methyladenosine (m6A) RNA modifications control the antiviral response to influenza A virus infection by limiting IFITM2/3 expression
abstract: N6-methyladenosine (m6A) RNA modifications regulate diverse cellular processes, including the response to virus infection. However, how m6A controls antiviral gene expression and whether effects on viral replication are due to direct modification of viral RNA or regulation of cellular transcripts remain unclear. Herein, we analysed how m6A modifications control the cell-autonomous innate immune response to influenza A virus (IAV) infection. Depletion or inhibition of the m6A writer METTL3 or the m6A reader YTHDF2 restricts IAV replication. However, using a quantitative method to identify m6A sites, we did not detect substantial m6A modification of viral RNA. In contrast, many IAV-induced cellular transcripts were m6A modified in their coding region, including those that encode pattern recognition receptors and direct antiviral proteins. Inhibition of interferon signalling restored IAV replication after METTL3 inhibition, highlighting that m6A controls the antiviral response to infection. METTL3 inhibition increased expression of the paralogous antiviral proteins IFITM2 and IFITM3, which were required for the antiviral activity of the METTL3 inhibitor. We propose that m6A modifications regulate the expression of antiviral proteins to limit the magnitude of their induction and balance antiviral activity with maintaining cellular homeostasis.

title_zh: N6-甲基腺苷(m6A)RNA修饰通过限制IFITM2/3表达调控抗病毒药物对流感A病毒感染的反应

abstract_zh: N6-甲基腺苷(m6A)RNA修饰调控多种细胞过程,包括对病毒感染的反应。然而,m6A如何调控抗病毒药物基因表达,以及其对病毒复制的影响是否源于病毒RNA的直接修饰或对细胞转录本的调控仍不清楚。在此研究中,我们分析了m6A修饰如何调控细胞自主的先天免疫应答对流感A病毒(IAV)感染的反应。METTL3或YTHDF2的耗尽或抑制会限制IAV复制。然而,使用定量方法识别m6A位点后,我们并未检测到病毒RNA的显著m6A修饰。相反,许多由IAV诱导的细胞转录本在其编码区被m6A修饰,包括编码模式识别受体和直接抗病毒药物蛋白的转录本。干扰素信号通路的抑制可恢复METTL3抑制后的IAV复制,这表明m6A调控了抗病毒药物对感染的反应。METTL3的抑制增加了同源抗病毒药物蛋白IFITM2和IFITM3的表达,这些蛋白对于METTL3抑制剂的抗病毒药物活性是必需的。我们提出,m6A修饰通过调控抗病毒药物蛋白的表达来限制其诱导的幅度,并在维持细胞稳态的同时平衡抗病毒药物活性。

title: B-312 Universal genotyping of Influenza A virus: an agile Oxford Nanopore Sequencing workflow using universal segment primers
abstract: Abstract Background Influenza A is a segmented negative-sense RNA virus with eight genomic segments. Efficient genome characterization is essential for molecular surveillance and public health decision-making. Universal primers targeting conserved terminal regions enable amplification of all segments within a single workflow, supporting rapid sequencing and genotype assignment. This study aimed to standardize and evaluate a universal-primer Oxford Nanopore workflow for Influenza A genotyping, including real-time monitoring and post-run clade assignment. Methods Residual eluates from respiratory samples collected between October and November 2025 that tested positive for Influenza A by qPCR were used for genomic surveillance. Samples were de-identified and submitted to cDNA synthesis (High-Capacity cDNA Reverse Transcription Kit) supplemented with universal primers targeting conserved terminal regions. Amplicon enrichment was performed with the same primer sets and Q5® High-Fidelity 2X Master Mix; products were assessed by agarose gel electrophoresis. Barcoding used a transposition-based approach, libraries were adapter-ligated, and sequencing was performed on MinION flowcells. Real-time monitoring was performed with RAMPART. Consensus generation was performed in EPI2ME, followed by clade/genotype analysis using Nextclade for Influenza A(H3N2) HA and NA against reference A/Darwin/6/2021. Results A library of 95 samples was sequenced for 5 hours and 31 minutes, generating 752,910 reads. Using predefined criteria for near-complete genome recovery (minimum 20× depth and =75% horizontal genome coverage), 71/95 samples met the established metrics. Four samples produced no mapped reads. The remaining 20 samples yielded partial genome recovery with mean horizontal coverage of 52% (range 8.08%–74.94%). Despite incomplete whole-genome recovery in a subset, clade-level genotyping was achieved for 87/95 samples (91.6%), indicating that sufficient subtype/clade-informative sequence was obtained for most specimens. Eight samples were not genotyped: four due to absence of mapped reads and four due to insufficient coverage to support confident assignment. Conclusion This universal-primer Nanopore workflow enabled rapid, high-throughput Influenza A genotyping with real-time monitoring and high clade-assignment success (91.6%) in a single MinION run. QC thresholds of 20× depth and =75% horizontal coverage effectively identified samples suitable for near-complete genome recovery, while clade assignment remained feasible for most samples despite heterogeneous input quality. This approach supports agile clinical-laboratory surveillance with scalable implementation.

analysis.summary_en: This study introduces a universal-primer Oxford Nanopore sequencing workflow for rapid and high-throughput genotyping of Influenza A viruses. The workflow uses conserved terminal region primers to amplify all genomic segments in a single process, enabling real-time monitoring and post-run clade assignment. A total of 95 respiratory samples collected between October and November 2025 that tested positive for Influenza A by qPCR were analyzed. Using predefined criteria for genome recovery, 71 samples met the metrics for near-complete genome recovery, while 20 samples had partial coverage. Four samples produced no mapped reads. Despite incomplete genome recovery in some cases, clade-level genotyping was achieved for 87 samples (91.6%). The study highlights the feasibility of this approach for scalable clinical-laboratory surveillance, supporting efficient molecular surveillance and public health decision-making. The workflow's effectiveness was demonstrated through real-time monitoring and clade assignment using Nextclade against reference A/Darwin/6/2021. The evidence is strong, with high confidence in the workflow's performance for Influenza A genotyping.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在标准化并评估一种针对流感A病毒基因型鉴定的通用引物牛津纳米孔测序工作流程,包括实时监测和运行后分支分配。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 样本去标识化后,使用High-Capacity cDNA Reverse Transcription Kit进行cDNA合成,并补充针对保守末端区域的通用引物。使用2025年10月至11月期间通过qPCR检测出流感A病毒的呼吸道样本残余洗脱液进行基因组监测。
